Quick start

How to use this tool

  1. Find the current grade for all work other than your final exam.
  2. Enter the course percentage you want to achieve and the final’s percentage weight from your syllabus.
  3. Calculate the required score. Switch modes if you already know your exam result.

Planning estimate · Check your syllabus for official grading rules.

See the formula ↓

How the calculation works

Required final score = (Target − Current × (1 − Weight / 100)) ÷ (Weight / 100)

A worked example

Your current grade is 85%, your target is 90%, and your final is worth 30%. The completed work contributes 85 × 0.70 = 59.5 percentage points. You need another 30.5 points: 30.5 ÷ 0.30 = 101.666…%. The displayed minimum is 101.67%. A target above 100% on the final is not reachable under an ordinary 0–100 grading rule.

Before you use the result

The required score is rounded upward to two decimal places so the displayed minimum does not fall below the mathematical target. Outcome comparisons are rounded to the nearest hundredth. A result below zero means a zero score would already meet your target mathematically; it does not remove attendance or exam-pass requirements. If the final belongs inside a test category, other work is still ungraded, or your school drops scores, this simple model is not enough.

Results display to two decimal places unless stated otherwise. Read our calculation methodology for scope and limitations.

Frequently asked questions

Does current grade include the final?

No. Use the grade for all non-final work, normalized to a percentage. A gradebook treating an ungraded final as zero is not the correct input.

What if I need more than 100%?

Your target is not reachable using an exam score capped at 100% under these assumptions. Check the weights and consider a lower target. Extra credit or retake policies are not modeled.

Can I calculate what I need to pass?

Yes. Enter your course’s actual passing percentage as the target. Separate must-pass exam requirements still apply.
